newsitem.title: USA: U.S. paper and pulp hikes set for July.
newsitem.headline: U.S. paper and pulp hikes set for July.

text.p: U.S. paper companies have raised prices in key product lines, leading many on Wall Street to believe that the recovery of the industry is coming earlier than expected.

International Paper raised prices on certain grades of pulp up to $50 a metric ton, effective June 1, and Stone Container Corp, Weyerhaeuser Co and Champion International Corp followed suit with similar increases effective July 1.

Georgia Pacific and Interntional Paper are asking higher prices for linerboard, while Union Camp said that effective August 1, it will raise the price of uncoated cut-sized white paper $50 a tonne, following earlier price hikes.
"We think the supply and demand fundamentals are there to support price recovery," said a Union Camp spokesman, and that feeling was echoed by others in the industry.
"It's a question of supply and demand and this is a cyclical industry," added a spokeswoman at Champion International, of its pulp increase.
She added that "in the last upturn pulp led the market. It was the first to start to move."
Those prices are helping push up stock prices in the producers as well, say analysts.
"Some stocks are starting to get back to their mid-1995 levels," said Mark Diverio at UBS Securities. "We're in the early stages of a paper industry recovery."
In trading late Wednesday, Weyerhaeuser was up 3 to 53-3/8, Georgia-Pacific climbed 1-3/8 to 88-1/8 and Boise Cascade moved up 1-1/4 to 38.
